frozen: 2026-10-16, in the first commit of this search, before any data below was pulled or read
asked: Davies, 2026-10-16: "ig除了澳元这个还有什么别的策略吗？再深度研究下，结合多个数据源，策略够好的话有一定风险会亏钱也没问题"
rule: Every rule, threshold, era boundary and cost below is fixed here. Nothing is tuned on the test era; a changed rule is a new proposal, and the old one is still reported. Every arm is reported, none dropped.

eras.note: a family whose data starts later uses its own split, stated in it; train and test are both reported, the verdict reads the test era

bar.candidate: test-era mean net of IG costs > 0 with t >= 2.5 AND train-era mean > 0 with t >= 2.0, AND the test-era bootstrap 95% lower bound > 0
bar.family_count_note: about 30 arms; t >= 2.5 on an out-of-sample era whose rule was fixed on the other era is the bar, not a Bonferroni over the whole search, because the test era is untouched by selection

bootstrap.unit: whole trades (or months for continuous strategies)

verdicts: worth small real money after demo
bar.small_money_needs: candidate bar met in both eras by two independent data sources, and a worst single loss Davies can fund at the minimum stake

ig_costs.source: IG UK product pages read 2026-10-15/16 (docs/agents/backtests/ig_deepdive/inputs/sources/ and this folder's inputs/sources/); spreads converted to bps at the levels stated per market

fx_dfb.note: F12 vs F13 disagree; both run

commodity_undated.note: market cost of carry plus 3 % (commodities page)

JP225.note: not read at source; the 2026-10-09 review's figure class, flagged

UST10.note: Treasury note futures bet row; spread from the bonds page class

ig_costs.levels_note: levels are round present-day values used only to turn point spreads into bps and minimum stakes into notional; each result says which level it used

TSMOM.rule: monthly, at each month's last trading day: position in each market = sign(trailing 252-day excess return) x min(2, 0.10 / sigma60), sigma60 the annualised 60-day stdev of daily excess returns; portfolio = average of the market positions (equal risk); held to the next month end
TSMOM.variant_ENS: the same with the sign replaced by the mean of the signs of the 21-, 63- and 252-day excess returns

sources.A: Yahoo daily (indices ^GSPC ^FTSE ^GDAXI ^N225; GC=F, CL=F; FX =X; ^TNX for yields) with FRED rates
sources.B: FRED daily (SP500 where it exists, DEX* FX, DCOILWTICO, DGS10) and Dukascopy daily candles (indices, XAUUSD)

TSMOM.excess_return: index price + assumed dividend yield (US 2 %, UK 3.5 %, DE 0 (performance index), JP 2 %) - local short rate; FX spot + (r_foreign - r_USD) from FRED 3-month interbank; gold spot - US rate; WTI front futures excluding roll days (|return| > 5 sigma on an expiry week is dropped, counted); UST10 from DGS10 by duration 8 (-D x dy + (y - rf)/252)
TSMOM.costs: each month: half-spread x |change in position| x 2 sides, plus the market's admin fee on |position| daily

PREFOMC.rule: long US500 from the close before a scheduled FOMC statement day to that day's close (one night funded)
PREFOMC.dates: fetched from federalreserve.gov (fomccalendars.htm and fomchistoricalYYYY.htm), scheduled meetings only

sources.B: FRED SP500 (2016 on) and Dukascopy USA500IDXUSD daily (2012 on)

TOM.rule: long US500, UK100 and DE40 from the close of the second-to-last trading day of each month to the close of the third trading day of the next (four trading days, nights funded as held)

sources.B: Dukascopy daily index CFDs (2012 on) and FRED SP500 (2016 on)

OVERNIGHT.rule: long US500 from the cash close to the next cash open (SPY close -> open), one night funded; and its control, open -> close

sources.B: Yahoo QQQ (a second market, same vendor) and Dukascopy USA500IDXUSD hourly 21:00 -> 14:30 UK

MONTHEND_FIX.rule: Melvin and Prins (2015): on the last London business day of each month, from 14:00 to 16:00 London, buy the foreign currency against USD if the US equity index outperformed the foreign one month-to-date (to the previous close), sell it otherwise. Pairs and indices: EURUSD/^GDAXI, GBPUSD/^FTSE, USDJPY/^N225 (USDJPY sold when the foreign currency is bought), AUDUSD/^AXJO

sources.B: the committed FXCM fix table (statarb_search2/inputs/fx/fxcm_*_fix.csv.gz: mids at London 14:00 and 16:00, 2016 on)

MONTHEND_FIX.costs: one IG average spread a round trip

SEASONAL.GOLD_SEP_NOV: long gold over September and over November (Baur 2013), funded as spot gold (tom-next + 1 %); one round trip each
SEASONAL.WTI_MAR_APR: long WTI from the first to the last trading day of March-April, funded as an undated commodity (3 %)
SEASONAL.eras: default (gold from 2000 on Yahoo, oil from 1986 on FRED)

sources.B: Dukascopy XAUUSD daily and FRED DCOILWTICO

SESSION.rule: Breedon and Ranaldo (2013): currencies weaken in their own trading hours. Daily: short EUR/USD and GBP/USD 07:00 -> 12:00 UK; long USD/JPY 00:00 -> 06:00 UK; short AUD/USD 23:00 -> 05:00 UK. No funding (no 22:00 crossing except AUD's leg, flat by 05:00, which does not cross 22:00)

sources.B: the committed FXCM fix table where its London times allow (none of these legs): single intraday source, said so

MONDAY_GAP.ESG: if |ln(Sunday first price / Friday last price)| >= 0.5 % on the S&P 500, fade it at the Sunday open and exit Monday 16:00 ET; neighbours 0.25 % and 0.75 %
MONDAY_GAP.FILL: the same entry, exit when the Friday close is touched, else Monday 16:00 ET
MONDAY_GAP.costs: US500 0.6 pt in, 0.4 pt out, no funding (opened after Sunday 22:00, closed before Monday 22:00)

VIX_CARRY.rule: short the front VIX future (Cboe settlements, committed) at each cycle start when front/spot VIX >= 1.05 and spot VIX < 20, a guaranteed stop at +50 %, notional 10 % of capital; IG's VIX market costs 0.1 point a side and a guaranteed-stop premium of 0.2 point when triggered

PEAD.rule: not run if no keyless earnings-surprise history is found; IG share CFD commission arithmetic reported instead

CROSS.COT_CONTRA: weekly: for gold, WTI, S&P 500 (E-mini), 10-year note, EUR, JPY: non-commercial net position as a share of open interest, its percentile over the prior 156 weeks; above 90 -> short the market for 4 weeks, below 10 -> long for 4 weeks (CFTC legacy futures-only reports, position known Tuesday, traded at Friday's close)
CROSS.REAL_YIELD_GOLD: monthly: long gold if the 3-month change in the 10-year real yield (FRED DFII10) is negative, short if positive
CROSS.CREDIT_EQUITY: daily signal, traded at the close: long US500 when the Baa - 10y Treasury spread (FRED DBAA - DGS10) is below its 126-day average, flat otherwise; compared with always long, both funded

PORTFOLIO.rule: equal-risk combination of every arm that meets the candidate bar, monthly returns, risk-scaled on the train era only

capital: for each survivor: the minimum stake's notional, the margin it needs, and the capital at which the worst historical month or trade costs no more than 20 % of it; expected GBP a year at that capital and at GBP 10,000, with the test era's bootstrap interval
term_9_12: each strategy is classed: can be run by hand from a published signal (daily or less often, or at a fixed clock time), or needs software (more than a few dealt trades a day, or reaction faster than a person)

deviations.written: 2026-10-16, before any result of the families it touches was computed
deviations.what: Dukascopy throttled this machine (HTTP 429 and dropped connections after a few dozen reads), so its hourly files cannot be read. FX hourly comes from FXCM's public weekly H1 bid/ask files, which start in 2012. MONTHEND_FIX and SESSION therefore split train 2012-01-01..2018-12-31 / test 2019-01-01..2026-10-15 on FXCM H1 (source A); MONTHEND_FIX's source B is the committed FXCM minute fix table (the same vendor, minute data, 2016 on); SESSION has one source.

With no Dukascopy hourly US 500 history, MONDAY_GAP has only Yahoo's 730 days of hourly ES=F (2024-05 on): one era. It is reported descriptively and its verdict is 'not run, coverage', as S3 of the IG verification was. OVERNIGHT's source B is QQQ (a second market on the same vendor) only.

Stooq refuses this machine's connections; it is not used. Dukascopy daily candles are read for USA500IDXUSD (2012 on) and XAUUSD (2003 on) only, the throttle allowing a few files a minute; UK 100, Germany 40 and Japan 225 have no source B, and WTI's source B is FRED.
